run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-14T18:43:39Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend-proxy RequestErrorRate alert is backed by observed error spans on frontend-proxy: its span error rate was ~0 through 18:46, peaked at ~2.05 spans/s at 18:50:39, and had fallen back to ~0.015/s by 18:58:39 (ERROR status, operations 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress'; 432 and 406 error spans respectively in a 25-minute increase). The individual error spans are HTTP 504 at 'ingress' with ~15.0s duration and 'router frontend egress' spans with error=true, http.status_code=0 and ~15.0s duration, i.e. frontend-proxy's 15s upstream timeout expiring on requests to frontend. A complete trace shows the delay originates below frontend: frontend 'GET /api/data' took 24.59s because its child 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' took 24.59s and the ad server span 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' took 22.37s, while ad's child client span to flagd 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean' waited 1.6-3.6s and flagd's own server span completed in 9 microseconds with 'context deadline exceeded' (grpc 2) — the request reached flagd long after ad had queued it. On the ad side the container was CPU-starved: the current ad pod's container burned ~0.049 cores against its 50m CPU limit and was throttled on 92-100% of CFS periods from its creation at 18:45 until ~18:55 (decaying to ~0.24-0.35 afterwards), while the previous ad pod had used 0.0035-0.008 cores and been throttled 5-14%, and ad's own span rate did not increase (1.7 spans/s at 18:46 vs ~2/s baseline, 0 during 18:50-18:52). Ad p95 latency rose from 88-195ms to 390ms and then 6834ms at 18:54:39, frontend 'GET /api/data' p95 rose from 167-354ms to 13499-14000ms, and frontend-proxy ingress carried a constant ~9.3-11.4 successful spans/s throughout, so this is latency/CPU starvation in ad, not a traffic surge. The alert rule itself is not loaded in this Prometheus, so its exact expression and the annotation value 2.4555 could not be verified.

claims.text: frontend-proxy span error rate was 0 until 18:46:39, rose to a peak of 2.048 error spans/s at 18:50:39, and fell to ~0.015/s by 18:58:39 (sum by status_code, rate over 5m).

In a 25-minute increase, frontend-proxy accumulated 432 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on span_name 'ingress' and 406 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on span_name 'router frontend egress' (plus ~10.3k UNSET spans each), while baseline error rate had been near zero.

The frontend-proxy error spans are HTTP 504 at 'ingress' with durations of ~15.0s (e.g. 15000561 us, 15000404 us) and 'router frontend egress' spans in the same traces with error=true and http.status_code=0 at ~15.0s, alongside a few 503 and 500 ingress spans; this is frontend-proxy's upstream timeout expiring, not an internal proxy error.

Trace d4057d2e24ea083d01006c39cd8fcd6a shows the chain: load-generator 'GET' 504 after 15.31s -> frontend-proxy 'ingress' 504 after 15.00s with child 'router frontend egress' 15.00s (http.status_code 0, error) -> frontend 'GET /api/data' 24.59s -> frontend 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' 24.59s -> ad 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' 22.37s (rpc.grpc.status_code 0).

In that same trace the delay is inside ad, not in flagd: ad's client spans 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean' took 1.60s, 3.60s and 2.30s with rpc.grpc.status_code 4 (deadline exceeded), while flagd's own server span of the same operation ran for 9 us starting ~2.6s after the ad client span began, carrying otel.status_description 'context deadline exceeded' and rpc.grpc.status_code 2.

The current ad pod's container was CPU-throttled on 92% of CFS periods at 18:45:30, reached 1.0 (100%) from ~18:51 to ~18:55, and decayed to 0.24-0.35 by 18:57-19:02; the previous ad pod measured 0.05-0.14 over 18:43-18:46 (rate over 2m, per pod, container='ad').

ad container CPU usage rose from 0.0035-0.0085 cores on pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc (18:24-18:46) to 0.035-0.049 cores on pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh (18:48-18:54), i.e. it saturated the 50m CPU limit in the deployment spec, while flagd's container was throttled 0% and frontend-proxy 0.03-0.06 and frontend 0.26-0.34 stayed flat across the window.

ad's span rate did not increase during the incident: 1.7 spans/s at 18:46:39 versus ~1.9-2.2/s earlier, and 0.007/s and 0/s at 18:50:39 and 18:52:39 (requests stalling inside ad), so the CPU burn was not caused by extra request volume.

ad server-span latency p95 for 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' was 88-195ms until 18:48:39, 390ms at 18:50:39, then 6834ms at 18:54:39, 1283ms at 18:56:39 and 724-782ms at 18:58-19:00, settling at 277-306ms at 19:01-19:03.

frontend 'GET /api/data' p95 was 167-354ms until 18:44:39, jumped to 13499ms at 18:54:39 and 13999ms at 18:56:39, then 342-358ms at 18:58-19:00, and frontend 'tcp.connect' error spans appeared only during the same period (0 before 18:46:39, 0.033-0.041 spans/s at 18:46-18:48, 0 again by 18:58).

frontend-proxy ingress request volume was unchanged: the STATUS_CODE_UNSET series stayed at 9.3-11.4 spans/s from 18:25 to 19:03 while the ERROR series went from 0-0.015/s to 0.211/s at 18:47, 0.837/s at 18:51 and back to 0.013/s at 19:01.

Error-status spans in the 20-minute window cluster on one path: frontend-proxy 'ingress' 434 and 'router frontend egress' 409, frontend 'GET /api/data' 408, 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' 408 and 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' 409 — i.e. the ads path only; other frontend operations (GET /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, grpc CartService/CheckoutService calls) show 0, and recommendation 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' shows 1.05 error spans.
The ad Deployment specifies container 'ad' with limits cpu=50m/memory=450Mi and requests cpu=10m/memory=225Mi, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad; the deployment is 1/1 ready.

The ad pod was replaced at 18:44:59-18:45:01 by its own controller (events SuccessfulCreate pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh, SuccessfulDelete pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc, Started container ad), with restart count 0 on the new pod and image digest sha256:c9d4f94314937eb3b61cf8b1672b7e87fab95442bd1d01f8d32f43a882255944.

Both ad ReplicaSets (ad-554b849958, replicas 0; ad-785b4464f5, replicas 1, created 18:44:59) have identical pod templates: image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, limits cpu 50m/memory 450Mi, requests cpu 10m/memory 225Mi.

ad container logs in the window show only normal request lines ('Targeted ad request received for [...]', 'Non-targeted ad request received', 'no baggage found in context'); no error, failure, panic or CPU-related lines appear in the 120 most recent of 340 lines read.

ad's container memory working set on the new pod grew from 74MB at 18:46 to 255MB at 18:50, 323MB at 18:54 and 333MB at 18:56 (plateau), staying under the 450Mi limit; the previous ad pod held a steady 322MB.
The flagd configuration ConfigMap currently defines flags adHighCpu (default off), adManualGc (default off) and adFailure (default on), among others, all state ENABLED.

Primary cause: ad's container was starved of CPU by its own 50m limit (CFS throttling 92-100% with usage pinned at ~0.049 cores from 18:45 onward), which delayed ad's request processing into multi-second latency, pushed frontend 'GET /api/data' beyond frontend-proxy's 15s upstream timeout, and produced the 504 error spans that raised the frontend-proxy RequestErrorRate alert.

Unresolved trigger: the ad pod created at 18:44:59 (ad-785b4464f5-9bshh) consumed roughly seven times the CPU of the pod it replaced (~0.049 vs 0.0035-0.008 cores) while serving no more requests, and its throttling started at creation; the pod template, image tag and resources are identical to the previous ReplicaSet, so what made the new process CPU-bound (for example a flag-driven CPU burn such as adHighCpu/adManualGc, or an unverified template/behaviour difference) cannot be determined from the available data.

flagd is not the latency source: flagd's container throttling ratio was 0 throughout the window, and its own ResolveBoolean server span executed in 9 us while the ad-side client span of the same call waited 1.6-3.6s before the request arrived.

frontend-proxy itself was not resource-constrained or volume-driven: its container throttling ratio stayed at 0.03-0.06 and frontend's at 0.26-0.34 across the whole window, and its ingress span rate was flat at ~9.3-11.4/s while only the error series rose.

Rejected: the fraud-detection pod's OOMKill explains this alert — its last termination was OOMKilled exit code 137 finishing at 18:19:37 (24 minutes before the ad error onset), it restarted once outside the error window, and the error-span query shows 0 error spans for fraud-detection's operations, so it is not tied to this failure path.

Raise or re-tune the ad container CPU limit (currently cpu=50m, which the current pod saturates with ~100% CFS throttling, and which the replacement pod still throttles 24-35% with residual ~280-310ms GetAds p95 versus a 90-190ms pre-incident baseline) and re-measure ad GetAds p95 and throttle ratio afterwards.

Pull the ad workload's change history for the 18:44:59 rollout (why a new ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5 was created with an identical pod template) and check whether flagd flag adHighCpu or adManualGc was switched to 'on' between ~18:45 and ~18:55; that history is not available in this Run.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not loaded in this Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name 'RequestErrorRate' and with type=alert both returned no data, so the rule expression, threshold and evaluation window behind the annotation value 'current: 2.4555555555555553' are unknown.

The annotation value 2.4555 could not be reproduced: the highest observed frontend-proxy span error rate in the window was 2.048 error spans/s (5m rate) at 18:50:39, and the alert reports the condition 'above 0', so the exact quantity and the reason the alert is recorded as starting at 18:43:39 (when frontend-proxy error rate was ~0.004-0.015/s) are unresolved.
The flagd container produced no readable log lines for 18:40-19:08 (all three containers returned no_data), so flagd-side diagnostic detail is missing.

The previous ad pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc was deleted, so its logs, image digest and per-request CPU profile cannot be compared with the replacement pod; only the ReplicaSet templates (identical) are available.

The values of the flagd flags adHighCpu, adManualGc and adFailure at 18:45-18:56 are unknown — only their current values in the flagd-config ConfigMap are visible, and change_history is not integrated in this Run.
No Kubernetes event or log explains the 18:44:59 ad ReplicaSet change beyond SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete/Started; the cause of that rollout is unknown.
ad 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' p95 is NaN (no computable value) at 18:51:39-18:53:39, so the peak latency of that operation between those samples is unknown.
Latency conclusions are limited by the absence of span-metric samples before 18:23:39 in the returned series; comparisons use the 18:23-18:46 stretch as the in-window baseline.
next_steps: Query the Alertmanager/Prometheus that actually holds the RequestErrorRate rule to read its exact expression and evaluation interval, and confirm whether its 'error rate' is a span-error rate per second or a ratio.
Use the platform's change-history integration to check for ad Deployment edits or flagd flag changes between 18:40 and 19:00 on 2026-11-14.
Re-check ad container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total ratio and GetAds p95 over the next 30 minutes to confirm whether the residual 24-35% throttling and ~300ms p95 persist after the incident.
If ad CPU demand remains elevated at low request rates, capture a CPU profile or enable ad service debug logging to identify the CPU-burning code path (e.g. flag evaluation or GC).
